title: RentRight — Trust-first rental marketplace
summary: Built a 0→1 rental marketplace that eliminates scams and hidden fees through verification and transparency.
subheading: From risky rentals to trusted apartment discovery
problem: Finding apartments in Nigeria is stressful and risky — renters face scams, hidden fees (30-50% extra costs), and inefficient offline processes. Most discovery happens via agents, WhatsApp, and word-of-mouth, leading to wasted visits and lack of trust.
approach: Led end-to-end product development: conducted market research, defined target users (young urban renters), used RICE/MoSCoW for prioritization, wrote PRD, and designed wireframes. Focused MVP on trust signals, full cost transparency, and in-app inspection booking.
outcome: Created a prototype marketplace where renters can discover verified apartments, see total move-in costs upfront, and book inspections directly. Demonstrated structured product thinking from research to prototype, emphasizing trust over volume.

title: SafeSignal — From PRD to Prototype
summary: Designed a safety incident reporting app that enables users to submit reports in under 60 seconds while feeling safe and confident, from initial PRD analysis through MVP prototype.
subheading: From barriers to reporting to a trustworthy incident reporting platform
problem: Many safety incidents go unreported due to slow systems, fear of exposure, lack of evidence capture, and insufficient reassurance. Users need a way to report quickly and discreetly while maintaining confidence in the process.
approach: Analyzed the provided PRD to identify core pain points across three user groups (students, business owners, residents). Used MoSCoW prioritization to define a focused MVP around a single outcome: enable incident submission in under 60 seconds. Translated requirements into a multi-step wizard flow, designed anonymous reporting as a core feature, and prototyped an end-to-end experience with both user and admin interfaces.
outcome: Created a clickable MVP prototype that validates the complete reporting loop — from user onboarding through incident submission, confirmation, and admin review. Demonstrated structured product thinking by defining success criteria, identifying key product decisions, and proposing a validation plan for testing with real users.
